note: The donor-hardware session, as gates a script can check. Nothing here claims a run works: it checks that a captured log proves what the plan says it proves, and it refuses to score a log as hardware evidence when it cannot tell.

log_shape.active_app: \AD102-UNLOCK\RUNnnnn.TXT on the USB stick, one file per boot, never overwritten
log_shape.read_only_diagnostic: \\GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the USB stick; the VRAM-block probe build also writes one \\PROM-ssss-bb-dd-f-nnnn.BIN per card it read, named after that card and that run, never overwritten

readonly_guide.title: Read-only hardware execution guide, step by step
intro: The sections after this one describe the gates. This one is the sequence that produces a log to score, for every image in the catalogue that writes nothing to the GPU, and names the fact in each log that a hardware-dependent item is waiting for.

Archived captures now include waived actuating boots as well as read-only and preparation runs. The U/P/I captures documented below exposed software/setup failures; they do not hardware-verify the subsequent fixes. Every tool in the chain prints `HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0`, and no captured log changes a row in `docs/readiness_status.json` by itself: a log is something a reviewer reads, not a flag this repository flips.
readonly_guide.naming: There is no script called `build-sign-stage` in this repository. Use `-Only <profile>` with its arguments to select one configuration. `-StageDrive <letter>` stages one application. `-ListConfigurations` lists the build configuration IDs that identify the log and receipt evidence. Ordinary runs copy the signed `EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI`; the waived one-target application can also use `-StageDxeCompanion` to build/sign its matching driver and stage `EFI\Drivers\AdaUnlockDxe.efi` for the I path. `src/Build-Sign-Deploy-UniversalGPU.ps1` is that command, and `docs/BUILD_SIGN_DEPLOY.md` is its user document.

preconditions.why: the programmer, the known-good firmware image and the SPI part number are on the bench before the first boot; none of the images below writes the GPU, but the bench rule does not depend on that
serial, slot, board model and the vendor tool's VBIOS version, so the BDF and device ID in the log can be tied to a piece of silicon afterwards
no `GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-*.TXT` and no `AD102-UNLOCK\RUN*.TXT` on the stick; a stale file is indistinguishable from a live one and `session_preflight.py` refuses a medium that carries one

for every stage: the serial and slot of every card in the machine, plus the ordered BDF list the image is built with. This fork runs an ordered list with one card active at a time, so a two-card machine is the ordinary case and the list, not the card count, is what has to be written down

after each candidate, boot Windows once and record the build, driver version and device status: the read-only images promise the card is untouched, and this is the observation that would notice if it were not

the signing certificate lives in WSL (`$HOME/secureboot-signing/uefi-db.key` and `.crt`) and the same certificate must be enrolled in the BIOS `db`; the script refuses to sign when it is not, unless you pass `-SkipDbCheck` and accept a receipt that reads `DB_ENROLLED=UNKNOWN`
every command is written from the repository root, with the signed outputs landing in `artifacts\signed`

steps.title: confirm the catalogue accepts the candidate
steps.expect: one `CATALOGUE ... variants=41 families=5` line, then a `VARIANT <id> PROFILE=<profile> SAFETY=<class> BINARY=<name>` line per image; `NOT_BUILDABLE` lines say what this tree cannot produce and why. The candidate must be listed with the safety class in the table below.
steps.if_not: a missing id is a catalogue problem, not a bench problem: fix the tree before touching the stick.

steps.title: build, sign and stage in one command
steps.expect: `VARIANT_BEGIN` for the one image, `SIGNING_CERTIFICATE ... DB_ENROLLED=TRUE`, the verified signed SHA-256, `STAGED diag-topology-log PATH=... DRIVE=G:`, and a final `STATUS=SIGNED=1 FAILED=0 ... HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0`. A stick holds one `BOOTX64.EFI`, so this is one candidate per stick: the previous image is backed up locally before it is replaced.

expect_tokens.token: STATUS={0} SIGNED={1} FAILED={2} SKIPPED={3} DB_ENROLLED={4} HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0 MATRIX={5}

steps.if_not: `Refusing to stage` names the safety class and the missing switch. `-AcceptActuatingDeploy` exists for images that write the GPU; no read-only candidate in this guide needs it. `-SignOnly` builds and signs without touching a stick.

steps.title: check the bench before the boot
steps.expect: `STICK FREE_OF_OLD_LOGS=1`, `IMAGE ... BYTES=... SHA256=...` for the file that will actually boot, the six `MANUAL` gates, and `PREFLIGHT_VERDICT=PASS ... CHECKS=2 HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0`. `--skip-profile` is right for every candidate here: the reviewed ESP profile belongs to the waived stages. Add `--assets AD102,GA102` once the run is meant to get past `EFI_CRC_ERROR`: the image reads the five pinned files from the stick's root and hashes each before use, and a 3080 boot reads `\AD102-ASSETS\gsp_ga10x.bin` through its manifest's alternate path, so the check names that dependency instead of leaving it to a later `Pinned asset unavailable` line.
steps.if_not: `STALE_LOGS=` with an `ACTION=` line means the medium is not empty: archive and wipe it (M3) rather than rebooting over an old log. `IMAGE EMPTY=1` or `PE_HEADER=0` means step 2 did not produce the file you think it did.

steps.title: boot the stick once, from the firmware boot menu
steps.expect: Choose the USB entry once and let the image run to its own end. Do not retry inside the same session: the image takes the first free number on the medium, starting at 0000, so a second boot writes a second file and the two are only distinguishable by their numbers and their contents. The read-only candidates print `GPU hardware untouched` and return, and the handoff candidates start Windows after the log is closed.
steps.if_not: a hang is a finding: power-cycle, keep the stick as it is, and record what the screen last showed. Nothing in a read-only session writes the card, so a hang here is a firmware or console fault, not a damaged GPU.

steps.title: capture the log, then empty the medium
steps.command:
$evidence = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ('donor-evidence\' + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'))
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $evidence | Out-Null
$log = Get-ChildItem G:\ -Filter 'GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-*.TXT' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -Last 1
Copy-Item -LiteralPath $log.FullName -Destination $evidence
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 (Join-Path $evidence $log.Name)
(Get-Content -LiteralPath $log.FullName | Measure-Object -Line).Lines
steps.expect: The file named by the log's own `LOG_FILE=` line is the one to copy (the numbers start at 0000 and count up; on a clean medium the first run is `-0000.TXT`). Copy it off before wiping anything, and record its SHA-256, byte count and line count next to the candidate id. Wipe the stick afterwards so the next candidate starts from an empty medium.
steps.if_not: an empty stick with no log means the image never reached its save step. The screen said why: the last line before it stopped is the finding, and there is nothing to score.

steps.title: score the log against the gates
steps.expect: one `GATE <id> STAGE=<stage> RESULT=PASS` line per gate in the stage, the `NOTE` advisories, the six `MANUAL` gates, the `NOT_PROVEN` list, and `RUN_LOG_VERDICT=PASS ... HARDWARE_VERIFIED=0 GATES=3 GATES_FAILED=0`. Exit code `0` means every gate in that stage passed; `1` names the first failure in `FIRST_FAILED=`.
steps.if_not: exit `2` is a missing log, exit `3` is a log carrying the fixture marker (a synthetic log can never score as hardware evidence), and exit `1` is a real gate failure: `FIRST_FAILED=` names it, and the gate's own paragraph above says what it does not prove. For `prep-selected` and `dxe-prep-selected` the same command takes `--stage prepare` and the app's numbered log.

readonly_guide.after_the_steps: That is the loop: build-sign-stage, boot once, capture, score. The verdict is written into the session record beside the candidate id and the goal it was collected for. It does not change `hardware_verified` for anything, and the next section says why: a green read-only log is a statement about one image on one machine, not about a card.

candidates.title: Device-specific GOP text output cycle with a USB log
candidates.summary: Records the exact text interface on each captured GOP and its GOP-consuming driver image. It then sends a label through each distinct available device text interface for two seconds. The owner must confirm which monitor showed each label. No GPU driver Stop or console route change occurs.

evidence.why: Identifies the exact GOP handle where SimpleTextOut is available and whether it matches the captured graphics endpoint.
Records the separate graphics-console driver candidate, its agent and image resolution. The UEFI opener graph does not prove which driver installed SimpleTextOut.
Shows how many direct device-specific text calls returned success; the owner must observe each physical screen before treating the result as a usable display route.

candidates.does_not_prove: that a successful OutputString call produced visible pixels, that an identified GOP consumer installed the text protocol, or that any GPU can be safely stopped or reattached. Screen contents change; GPU configuration and firmware console ownership do not.

candidates.title: topology with a numbered USB log
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The baseline read-only contact: PCI tree, GPU identities, GOP and console ownership, one numbered log. This is the image the R1-R3 gates were written for.

evidence.why: names the configured-console finding on the machine in front of you: whether an AMD display function owns the console, or an NVIDIA path is configured and blocks it
the error-console half of the same question: an independent AMD `ErrOut` observation is what a console-handover refactor would rest on

evidence.token: GPU[%zu] BDF=%04x:%02x:%02x.%u ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x PCI_INDEX=%zu PARENT=%zu ROOT_PORT=%zu DEPTH=%u ANCESTRY=%u ROOT_VALID=%u GOP_COUNT=%u
evidence.why: one line per GPU with its GOP count, so the surviving-non-target-GOP question B2 is about is answered for this cabling instead of assumed
a numbered log written by an image launched from USB is the writable-medium half of B9 observed rather than assumed

evidence.token: PCI[%zu] %04x:%02x:%02x.%u %04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x CLASS=%04x ROOTPORT=%u PRIMARY=%02x BUSWINDOW=%02x-%02x BY_DRIVER=%u KNOWN=%u AGENT=%p PATH=%zu
evidence.why: device and subsystem id of every PCI node: the identity row a per-SKU entry (AD104/AD106/AD107, other GA102 ids) starts from

candidates.does_not_prove: that the card can be detached, unlocked or flashed: every eligibility flag in the log is zero by construction, and the report ends with `GPU hardware untouched`.

candidates.title: topology with a log and automatic Windows handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The same report, then the explicitly pinned Windows Boot Manager. The added value is not the topology: it is the observation that the reviewed ESP GUID boots Windows on this machine, after the log is closed.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID, and the image states it neither resets nor rewrites BootOrder

evidence.token: Starting the explicitly pinned Windows Boot Manager directly.
evidence.why: the line that must be followed by a Windows boot: the reviewed GUID is right only if Windows actually starts
the log is durably written before the handoff begins, so a failed handoff still leaves the evidence

candidates.does_not_prove: that the GUID names the only Windows loader, or that BitLocker, Secure Boot policy or anti-cheat accept that path (E10); it shows one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: selected-GPU observation with a log
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The passive diagnostic with an ordered selection: one snapshot, every requested BDF resolved before any report, then per-target identity and a summary. This is the read-only image that says something about two cards.

evidence.why: the requested BDF resolved to a device and subsystem id from the live snapshot: the runtime selector's positive case on real handles
a wrong or absent BDF refuses the whole sequence with no partial selection: the negative half of the same feature

evidence.token: SELECTION_STEP[%zu]=PASSIVE_IDENTIFIED ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x CLASS=%04x ROOT_INDEX=%zu DEPTH=%u GOP_COUNT=%u BY_DRIVER=%u OPENERS_KNOWN=%u
evidence.why: one numbered report per selected card in order, with its own GOP count and driver-owner status: the per-card data a multi-GPU refactor has to be written against

evidence.token: SELECTION_SEQUENCE=PASSIVE_IDENTIFIED COMPLETED=%u NON_SELECTED_NVIDIA_COUNT=%zu TOPOLOGY_VERDICT=%d CAN_DETACH=0 CAN_UNLOCK=0 CAN_FLR=0
evidence.why: the aggregate says how many NVIDIA cards were seen but not selected, which is the peer set the interference question is about

candidates.does_not_prove: that two cards can be actuated in order: the sequence is CPU-side reporting over one immutable snapshot, and B10's memory cost per additional card is untouched by it.

candidates.title: MSI B850 ROM variables
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: Reads the MS-7E56 firmware's `ROM_CMN`/`CSM_CMN` variables and dumps them raw, on the board fingerprint the earlier console analysis was done on. This is the only passive route to the firmware's own display-selection policy; it changes nothing.

evidence.why: the probe only runs on the exact board and GPU fingerprint, and it says in the same line that SMBIOS and the BIOS version are not verified

evidence.token: MSI_B850_VARIABLE NAME=%s EFI_STATUS=%#llx BYTES=%zu ATTRS=%#x CAP=%u RAW_ONLY=1 READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: the raw bytes of the variable, with `RAW_ONLY=1`: the firmware's display policy is in there, and the log does not pretend to interpret it
the line that bounds the probe: no vendor callback, no list traversal, no GPU action, so the dump cannot have changed the console state it describes

candidates.does_not_prove: which byte is `Initiate Graphic Adapter`, or that clearing it in firmware would give an AMD-exclusive `ConOut`/`ErrOut`: the dump is raw, there is no schema, and nothing here authorises an NVRAM rewrite.

candidates.title: MSI B850 ROM variables with handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The ROM-variable dump plus the pinned Windows handoff, so a passive capture of the firmware's display policy does not end with the operator hunting for a boot entry.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID and does not touch BootOrder
the dump is written before the handoff, so the evidence survives a handoff that fails

candidates.does_not_prove: anything the base ROM-variable probe does not prove, plus the handoff's own limit: one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: MSI B850 fuse version
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: One 32-bit read of the GSP fuse register per identity-verified card, plus one of the SEC2 register, and nothing else. The only image that reports which firmware signature slot a physical card's fuse selects.

evidence.token: MSI_B850_FWSEC_FUSE GPU=%s STATUS=OBSERVED BAR0_OFFSET=0x8241e0 RAW=%#x LOW16=%#x FUSE_VERSION=%u ARCHIVED_ROM_SIG_MASK=%#x CANDIDATE_SLOT=%u ARCHIVED_SLOT_NONZERO=%u ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
evidence.why: the fuse word and the slot it implies for each card: the per-card half of the Booter/V67/ROM pairing question, and the line ends `ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED`

evidence.token: MSI_B850_FWSEC_FUSE_BEGIN SOURCE=NOVA_CORE_GA102_PLUS READ_ONLY=1 CAN_DETACH=0 CAN_UNLOCK=0 NO_STOP=1 NO_DMA=1 NO_RESET=1
evidence.why: the first line of the probe says it reads only, so it can never establish firmware acceptance: C3 stays where it is whatever the value is

evidence.token: MSI_B850_SEC2_FUSE_BEGIN SOURCE=NOVA_CORE_GA102_PLUS REFERENCE_BOOTER=LINUX_610_43_03 ENGINE_MASK=0x1 UCODE_ID=3 WINDOWS_61742_DESCRIPTOR=UNKNOWN READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: the probe names the reference it decoded against (the Linux 610.43.03 header) and states that the Windows 617.42 descriptor is unknown: the asset-coupling claim, bounded in the log

candidates.does_not_prove: that the slot this fuse names is the slot Windows 617.42 selects; the same line prints `WINDOWS_61742_SIGNATURE_SLOT=UNKNOWN`, and no signature is authenticated anywhere in this path.

candidates.title: MSI B850 fuse version with handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The fuse read plus the pinned Windows handoff: a card that is left alone still has to end the session in Windows, and this is the variant that says so in one boot.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID and does not touch BootOrder
the fuse reads are written before the handoff begins

candidates.does_not_prove: anything the base fuse probe does not prove, plus the handoff's own limit: one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: MSI B850 SEC2 ucode version
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: One read of the SEC2 version register at BAR0+0x824140 per card, named as the Windows 617.42 register by the Linux 610.43.03 header. It reports a version and refuses to infer a signature from it.

evidence.token: MSI_B850_SEC2_UCODE1 GPU=%s STATUS=OBSERVED BDF=0000:%02x:00.0 BAR0_OFFSET=0x824140 RAW=%#x LOW16=%#x FUSE_VERSION=%u ENGINE_ID=1 UCODE_ID=1 SELECTED_SIGNATURE=UNVERIFIED SECURE_ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: the SEC2 version per card, with the selected signature and the secure-acceptance result stated as unverified in the same line
the completion line says how many of the expected reads landed and that no GPU write happened: a failed read is visible as a count, not as a silent zero

candidates.does_not_prove: that this version is the one Windows 617.42 uses. The register is named by a Linux header, the log prints `SELECTED_SIGNATURE=UNVERIFIED`, and the Windows signature slot stays `UNKNOWN`.

candidates.title: MSI B850 SEC2 ucode version with handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The SEC2 read plus the pinned Windows handoff, for a bench where the read-only image is expected to return to Windows by itself.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID and does not touch BootOrder
the read is written before the handoff begins

candidates.does_not_prove: anything the base SEC2 probe does not prove, plus the handoff's own limit: one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: read-only probe of the actuating write set
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: Forty-two BAR0 reads per verified card, at the addresses the waived transaction writes, plus the twenty-four words it reads without writing - the two HwCfg words `falcon_reset()` polls, the RISC-V halt word, the GFW and WPR2 bookkeeping words, and the rest of the set whose refused read stops the transaction. It is the interlock for the first actuation: run the same image before and after, and any block that moved shows up as a different digest. Nothing is written. It also copies the one-megabyte ROM window at BAR0 + 0x300000 and applies the same structural check the transaction applies before it refuses a board.

evidence.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_BEGIN SOURCE=UNLOCK_610_WRITE_SET BLOCKS=%u CONTEXT=%u MODE=READ_ONLY READ_ONLY=1 NO_STOP=1 NO_DMA=1 NO_RESET=1 NO_UNLOCK=1 NO_FLR=1 CAN_DETACH=0 CAN_UNLOCK=0 CAN_FLASH=0 NO_GPU_WRITES=1
evidence.why: the probe declares what it is before it reads anything: a read-only boundary and the size of its own address list, so a run that reads fewer blocks than the table has is visible in the first line rather than by counting the middle.

evidence.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE GPU=%s BDF=0000:%02x:00.0 BLOCK=%s BAR0_OFFSET=%#x ROLE=WRITE STATUS=OBSERVED RAW=%#010x ACCESS=%s READ_ONLY=1 ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
evidence.why: one line per word the actuating sequence writes: block name, the absolute BAR0 address, and the value there before any write exists. Forty-two of them (twenty per engine plus both selectors) is the evidence that this image addresses the same blocks as the transaction. It does not move C5: a readable address identifies the target, and there is no post-state yet to verify.

evidence.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_CARD GPU=%s READ=%u FAILED=%u OBSERVED=%u NOT_ACCESSIBLE=%u WRITE_SET_SHA256=%s DIGEST_CV=CHANGE_DETECTOR_ONLY ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED
evidence.why: the per-card digest is labelled a change detector in the line itself, and the line carries the failed-read count beside it: a digest over a partial read set would otherwise look complete. A digest over register values is not firmware acceptance, so C3 stays where it is.

evidence.token: VRAM_BLOCK_PROBE_END CARDS=%u BLOCKS=%u CONTEXT=%u EXPECTED_READS=%u READS_SUCCEEDED=%u READS_FAILED=%u DIGESTS=%u NO_GPU_WRITES=1 SECURITY_ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED OBSERVED=%u NOT_ACCESSIBLE=%u
evidence.why: the totals: cards probed, expected reads, reads that landed and reads that did not. A block that does not read back is a number here instead of a silent gap, which is the whole point of probing before the first write.

candidates.does_not_prove: that these are the right addresses for the transaction - only that this image and `src/vendor/unlock_610.c` name the same ones, checked by `tests/test_vram_block_probe.py`, not by the log. A successful read proves the word is reachable through PCI I/O; it does not prove an engine mask, a signature selector or a speed-selector write is permitted on this board, and it cannot say what any value means. The post-actuation half of the comparison has never run, because the actuation has never run.

candidates.title: read-only probe of the actuating write set, with handoff
candidates.log: \GPU-TOPOLOGY-DIAGNOSTIC-nnnn.TXT at the root of the stick, written by the image itself
candidates.summary: The block probe plus the pinned Windows handoff, for a bench where the read-only image has to return to Windows by itself. The end-of-session digest is in the log either way.

evidence.token: WINDOWS_HANDOFF=REQUESTED; pinned Windows ESP, no reset/BootOrder write
evidence.why: the handoff is pinned to one ESP GUID and does not touch BootOrder
the block lines and the digest are written before the handoff begins, so the evidence survives a handoff that does not

candidates.does_not_prove: anything the plain block probe does not prove, plus the handoff's own limit: one pinned partition started Windows once.

candidates.title: preparation for explicit targets, one or both cards
candidates.log: \AD102-UNLOCK\RUNnnnn.TXT, one file per boot, never overwritten
candidates.summary: The active application, built without the waiver: it runs the real inventory and selection, prepares its state, and refuses before `GuInit`. This is the only image here that executes the app's own entrypoint on hardware, which is why it is the one the P gates score. Given both BDFs it does the same thing for two cards in one boot: `GU_ACTIVE_SEQUENCE_PREPARE_ONLY` returns before the `MULTI_TARGET_WITHOUT_WAIVER` check, so preparing an ordered list needs no waiver - executing one does.

evidence.why: the app's inventory, selection and preparation completed on real firmware and the log says mutation was not authorised: the manual loop D5 says does not exist, run once, by hand
the app's own launch decision, printed before anything else: the USB-launch requirement observed rather than inferred

evidence.token: BOOT_STATE PRESENT=1 PHASE=%u BOOT_COUNT=%u STATUS=%#llx DEVICE=%04x
evidence.why: the persistent record is read at boot on real firmware, so a later boot's `PRESENT=1` is a record this tree wrote, not a fixture
building for one BDF and booting with a different card produces this refusal: the negative case of the image-refuses-a-card-it-was-not-built-for rule

evidence.token: ACTIVE_GPU[%zu] BDF=%04x:%02x:%02x.%u ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x CLASS=%04x LEGACY_UNLOCK_DEVICE_ID=%u
evidence.why: the identity the app itself resolved, with the device id it would act on: the first row of a per-SKU entry
how many NVIDIA cards the app saw, and how many of them the build asked for: the two numbers M4's record has to agree with before the ordered list is trusted

evidence.token: ACTIVE_PREPARED_STEP[%zu] BDF=%04x:%02x:%02x.%u ID=%04x:%04x SUB=%04x:%04x LEGACY_UNLOCK_DEVICE_ID=%u READ_ONLY=1
evidence.why: one line per selected card, in the order the selection names them: two of them is what a two-card session looks like, and their IDs are what ties each step to silicon

`PreparePlatformContexts` allocates one platform context per selected card and refuses an alias to the active context or a duplicate pointer, so two of these lines are evidence that two distinct per-card contexts existed at the same time in a read-only build
the cards were re-read after preparation and the revalidation passed: the log shows the second observation, not only the first

candidates.does_not_prove: that the ordered list may execute. Preparation and execution are different admissions: executing more than one target requires `-AcceptUnverifiedActuation` (`MULTI_TARGET_WITHOUT_WAIVER` otherwise), and nothing in a preparation log exercises a write, a Stop, a detach, a reset or a FLR. Two prepared contexts prove a list was built, not that a peer card is undisturbed during a multi-target mutation. RUN0031 separately records an operator-confirmed single-target 4090 mutation, not execution of this ordered two-target list.

candidates.title: DXE preparation for explicit targets
candidates.log: \AD102-UNLOCK\RUNnnnn.TXT, one file per boot, never overwritten
candidates.summary: The same preparation as a boot-service driver, loaded from a `Driver####` entry instead of `EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI`. It answers one question the application cannot: whether the same preflight runs under a driver loaded at `ReadyToBoot`.

evidence.why: both entrypoints call `GuDiscoverSingleGpu`, which refuses there; that shared boundary is what a resident-driver design has to be built on. Neither entrypoint's own banner can print in this build - `ACTIVE_APP=` in `src/app.c` and `ACTIVE_DXE=` in `src/dxe_main.c` both sit behind the `GuDiscoverSingleGpu` success check that refuses

candidates.does_not_prove: that the driver is safe to leave installed, or that `ReadyToBoot` timing is compatible with anything: the catalogue refuses to stage a DXE driver as `BOOTX64.EFI`, so the only path is a `Driver####` entry you add and remove by hand, and that is a firmware change, not a read-only act.

unscoreable.why: no `-SaveLog`: it prints to the console and writes nothing. A photograph of a screen is not a log, and `verify_run_log.py` scores files: use `diag-topology-log`, which is the same report with the save compiled in.
compile-only (`may_be_staged` is false): the image returns before any firmware or GPU operation, and CI already builds it. A boot would add nothing a compile does not already prove.
compile-only, as above: it exists to prove the ordered sources compile together.
compile-only DXE: nothing runs, so there is no log to score.
compile-only DXE, as above.
writes the GPU: this is the `actuate` stage, needs `-AcceptActuatingDeploy`, and is outside a read-only session by definition.
writes the GPU, ordered over several cards: `actuate` stage, and it needs the selection to be exactly what the catalogue says.

DXE Stop/release-only test, dynamically selecting supported NVIDIA GPUs by default with optional fixed BDF selection. No firmware asset files, PROM reads, or firmware unlock transaction; it returns to firmware after attempting reattachment. stages.what_it_costs: nothing: the diagnostic never writes a GPU register, resets a Falcon, calls the vendor Stop or loads firmware

stages.title: Preparation only
stages.what_it_costs: the active app runs its preflight and preparation, logs a refusal before any mutation, and hands back to Windows
stages.exit: preparation completes with MUTATION_AUTHORIZED=0 and no Stop, no waiver and no step line
stages.build_note: a selection without -EnableSingleTargetExecution and without the waiver compiles the preparation-only image (GPU-ACTIVE-PREP-*), which refuses to actuate before it starts

stages.title: Admission of a waived image, refused before mutation

stages.exit: the waived image prepared both cards, applied its admission policy, refused with a named reason, and the boot ended with nothing mutated, retained or faulted

go_no_go.summary: One stage's gates passing is not permission to run the next stage. This tool composes the stage verdicts into a single go/no-go answer and is the only thing in the repository that does so.
rules: the read-only stage must pass before preparation counts as done, and preparation must pass before actuation may be attempted at all

every stage must identify the same ordered target list: the list the first stage names (`SELECTION_REQUEST[n]`, `ACTIVE_PREPARED_STEP[n]`, `PASSIVE_SELECTION=`) must be the list every later stage names, in the same order, every card in it must appear in the read-only census, no card may appear twice, and the PCI id printed beside each BDF must agree across stages. A session where no stage names a target and the machine has more than one card is refused rather than guessed at: an ordered list of two cards is a normal session in this fork, an unnamed one is not
every manual gate must be acknowledged by its exact id; an unknown id is refused, so a typo cannot silently stand in for M6
a log carrying the fixture marker is refused (exit 3) unless --self-test is given, and a GO from a self-test still prints SYNTHETIC=1

captured_runs.title: Captured runs, scored
captured_runs.note: Physical runs, stored as files and scored by the same tool an operator runs. Each entry pins the digest of the stored log, the facts quoted from it, and the verdict line the verifier prints for it, and `tests/test_hardware_session.py` re-scores the file on every run: the record cannot drift from the evidence, and a gate that no healthy machine can satisfy fails the suite instead of the operator. The read-only runs and the preparation runs are scored per stage; `tools/donor_gate.py` is what composes them into a go/no-go answer.

runs.history: First run of the block probe, and the first read-only image here that reads the transaction's own address list. It answers the question it was built for: 88 of 88 reads landed on both cards, so the forty-two words `src/vendor/unlock_610.c` writes are all addressable through PCI I/O on this machine. It also found something the plan did not have. On both cards the five falcon-bridge words read as state, while the rest of the SEC2 window - and, on the 4090, nearly all of the GSP window as well - returns `0xbadf5620`, which is the shape `inaccessible()` treats as a refused read: 45 of the 84 write-set words across the two cards. The probe as built printed those as `STATUS=OBSERVED`, so section 11.33 teaches it to classify them, adds the two `HwCfg` words `falcon_reset()` polls before its first write, and records the finding here.
runs.does_not_show: that the actuating image will see the same values. It reads through the same `Mem.Read` call with the same width and bar index (`src/port.c`'s `GuRead32For`), so the values should reproduce, but that image has never run. It does not say why the engine refuses those words, or how a run would lift the refusal; and `0x8400f4`, the word `falcon_reset()` polls first, was not in the probed set, so whether the transaction stops at that poll or gets as far as its first write is still open.

runs.history: The read-set build of the probe. -0006 answered whether the words the transaction writes are addressable; this run answers whether the words it reads are readable, and with it the question -0006 left open: falcon_reset()'s first poll, 0x8400f4, reads 0x67b7 on the 4090 and 0x47f7 on the 3080, both as state. With bit 31 clear the pre-reset wait is the tolerated timeout the code's own comment describes, and with bit 12 clear the post-reset release wait is satisfied by the value that was already in the register, so it does not demonstrate that a reset happened. Two of the twenty-four new words are refused: SEC2.IRQSTAT on both cards, which only log_falcon_state() reads, and the 4090's GSP.RISCV halt word. Everything the layout and entry gates demand by exact value is present on both cards - PLM 0xffffff8f, GFW.PLM 0x8b8f, GFW.BOOT 0x3ff, GSP.CPUCTL 0x10, WPR2 high 0 - and the sixty-six write-set words are unchanged from -0006, digest included.
runs.does_not_show: that either card can be actuated. The probe reads and never resets, so the two refused words have no cause attached, and whether a refused word is refused again after an engine reset is exactly what only an actuating run can say. Nothing here touches the ROM window at BAR0+0x300000, which is the first content gate the transaction passes through, nor the profile and entry-selector bookkeeping the entry gate also requires. `ACCEPTANCE=UNVERIFIED` stands: a word that reads as state is not a signature check.

stopped_runs.title: Runs that stopped without terminating
stopped_runs.note: A boot that ends mid-file is evidence, and it is the kind that used to survive only as a message in a chat. These entries pin the digest and the facts of a run that did not finish, and they carry no gate claim: `tests/test_hardware_session.py` re-scores each one and fails the suite if any of them ever reads PASS. The bucket is separate from the captured runs on purpose - `captured_runs` exists to show that the gates *are* satisfiable by a healthy boot, so a run that stopped belongs here and not there. The first actuate stage that satisfied all five gates is not a single file: A5 needs the boot after, so `physical-actuate-0002` (the U boot) and `physical-actuate-0004` (the boot whose record shows what came of it) are scored together by the suite, and it re-scores both halves alone to show neither is the stage.
